findings: DMG matching is normalized name equality or contained application name of at least four characters, not bundle/signature/content identity. Unknown filename version can still produce a redundant-installer result.
trash checks only installer-path existence and does not revalidate receipt, installed application, version, source identity or contents. No installer or cleanup method was run.

Package matching examines only first eight listed Distribution/PackageInfo entries, then checks discovered identifiers against receipts. Incomplete metadata discovery can omit additional package components despite comments saying every identifier is checked.

Metadata parsing uses regex double-quoted attributes and identifier contains-dot heuristic, not full XML validation. Deduplication chooses first seen identifier across files rather than strongest required version.
Installed app inventory reads Applications and one nested level, accepts app-shaped entries with fallback names even if plist absent; read failures silently become empty inventory.

Subprocess deadline and output cap are checked after blocking reads; terminate followed by waitUntilExit is not an independent timeout bound. Metadata entries are passed to xar extraction without local canonical containment validation in this source.
Version comparison uses Foundation numeric string comparison, not explicit semantic-version policy. This workflow identifies installation redundancy, not file duplicates.
